style: Say clearly and kindly, like a patient elementary school teacher
lines: Welcome to Melt or Not! We will change things, then test if they can go back.
Can it go back to how it was?
You predicted: it can go back. Let's test it!
You predicted: it can't go back. Let's test it!
What did we find out?
Melting and freezing can go back. Cooking, baking and burning cannot.
An ice cube. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's a puddle of water.
The water froze into ice again!
Melting and freezing can go back and forth.
A slice of bread. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's toast.
Still toast! Cooling it down does not make it bread again.
Toasting changes bread for good.
A chocolate bar. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's melted chocolate.
The chocolate turned solid again!
It is a new shape, but it is still chocolate, and it can melt again.
A raw egg. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's a fried egg.
Still a fried egg! It will never be runny again.
Cooking changes an egg for good.
A cup of orange juice. What happens if we cool it down?
Now it's an ice pop.
The ice pop melted back into juice!
Freezing and melting can go back and forth.
Popcorn kernels. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's popped popcorn.
Still popcorn! Popped corn cannot pop back into kernels.
Popping changes corn for good.
A stick of butter. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's melted butter.
The butter turned solid again!
Butter melts when warm and turns solid when cool.
Cake batter. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's a cupcake.
Still a cupcake! Baking cannot be undone.
Baking changes batter for good.
A ball of clay. What happens if we roll it?
Now it's a clay snake.
It is a ball again!
Changing the shape of clay can go back.
A sheet of paper. What happens if we warm it up?
Now it's burned paper.
Still ash! Burned paper cannot turn back into paper.
Burning changes paper for good. (Only grown-ups do this, and only safely!)
